title: Hud and his people
hook: Hud tells 'Ad to ask forgiveness and He'll add strength to strength (11:52)

segments.voice: Yesterday, the ark in full, and Nuh's words at boarding. Your line was in his name it sails and anchors. Did one trip get a breath at the start and the end? Day four hundred thirty-five.
screen: `IN HIS NAME IT SAILS AND ANCHORS.`

segments.voice: You've met the people of 'Ad before, back in al-A'raf: the tower builders of ancient Arabia, proud of their strength, and the prophet sent from among them, Hud. Surah Hud carries his name, and it gives his preaching more room. Here is a man standing up in a town where everyone is bigger, richer and louder than he is. He has nothing they need. They have wealth, fortresses, numbers. And what he tells them is that the way to become even stronger is to do the one thing strong people find hardest.

Hud begins the way Nuh began before him in this surah: my people, worship God; you have no god but Him. I ask you no wage for this, he says; my wage is only from the One who made me. Then something that sounds almost like a business proposal, in verse fifty-two, in paraphrase: my people, ask forgiveness of your Lord, then turn back to Him. He will send the sky down on you in abundant rain, and add strength to your strength. Notice who he's talking to. Not weak people. A people already famous for strength. And he doesn't tell them to give it up. He tells them how to get more. In this verse, asking forgiveness isn't a loss of face. It's a source of power. The rain matters too: for people in a dry land, rain is life. The same promise appears in another surah, on Nuh's lips: ask forgiveness, and He will send rain and help you with wealth and children. The people of 'Ad answer: you've brought us no clear sign; we won't abandon our gods on your word. Some of our gods must have touched you with madness. Hud doesn't flinch. He says, in paraphrase: I trust in God, my Lord and yours. There is no living creature He does not hold by its forelock. Commentators picture a horse led by the hair above its brow. Every creature, every tower builder, is held. In the end, Hud and those with him were saved, the surah says, by a mercy from God, and 'Ad were followed by a curse in this world. The one thing the strong couldn't do, the thing that would have made them stronger, was to say: forgive me.
screen: `MY PEOPLE, ASK FORGIVENESS.` · `RAIN, AND STRENGTH TO YOUR STRENGTH.` · `HELD BY THE FORELOCK.` · `THE STRONG WOULD NOT SAY IT.` · then, large: `FORGIVENESS IS STRENGTH.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: ask forgiveness for strength. Sit, and breathe. Think of one place where you've been holding on to being right, where saying sorry would feel like losing. Notice how much effort it takes to keep holding. Now imagine putting it down. If you pray, you can say astaghfirullah slowly, a few times, I ask God's forgiveness, and notice what happens in your shoulders. If not, simply rehearse, in your mind, the honest sorry you could say. The bell holds the time.
Hud and his people. The prophet who told the mighty people of 'Ad that asking forgiveness would add strength to their strength. Today's word.
Your line: forgiveness is strength. Today, say one sorry you've been holding back, or ask forgiveness, in whatever way is yours. Day four hundred thirty-five.

howItsDone: Muslim teachers encourage saying astaghfirullah, I ask God's forgiveness, often through the day, and cite Hud's words in 11:52 and Nuh's in 71:10–12 for the blessings tied to seeking forgiveness, including rain and strength.

myth: Hud tells 'Ad to give up their strength
he promises asking forgiveness will add strength to their strength.
the promise of rain for seeking forgiveness also appears with Nuh
in Surah Nuh: ask forgiveness, and He will send rain and help you.
Hud asked 'Ad for a reward for his message
he says: I ask no wage of you; my wage is only from the One who made me.

fork.setup: you're a prophet speaking to a people proud of their strength. how do you tell them to grow even stronger?
options: ask forgiveness and turn back to God.
fork.reveal: ask forgiveness, then turn back: He will send rain in abundance and add strength to your strength (11:52).

original.note: Arabic: "strength to your strength," Hud's promise in 11:52.

trapdoor: what you thought: an ancient people punished for idol worship.
what it means: a prophet telling the strong that asking forgiveness is where more strength comes from.
what a scholar hears: 11:52 pairs istighfar with tawba and promises rain, echoing 71:10–12; 11:56's forelock (nasiya) image is used elsewhere for God's full control.

notes: All Qur'an references paraphrased; confirm the paraphrases of 11:51, 11:52, 11:53–54, 11:56 and 11:58–60.
Day 409 (al-A'raf) already covered 'Ad's towers, Iram and the wind; this day stays with Hud's words in Surah Hud (forgiveness as strength, the forelock) and refers back.
